observation.visible_scene: A close, static shot of an open upright piano: a tan-and-white guinea pig lies stretched out on a folded white towel placed directly on the left portion of the keyboard, while a person's two hands play the keys on the right. The piano's internal action (hammers, strings, dampers) is visible in the background, and the glossy black fallboard/lid above the keys reflects the guinea pig and the player's forearm.
visible_changes: Throughout the excerpt the player's hands keep moving over the keys: the right hand's fingers press and release the black keys, shifting position along them (e.g., a clearly blurred right-hand motion around t=0.27, and the index finger extended onto a black key in the later frames t=1.2–2.7), while the lower left hand's fingers press the white keys.
The guinea pig stays lying in the same pose on the towel for the whole segment, head resting on the towel fold, with no locomotion; only negligible body/eye motion is discernible.
The reflection on the polished lid shifts in step with the moving arm/hand, but it is a mirror image, not a second animal or hand.
The keyboard, towel, guinea pig and background action hold fixed positions in the frame, indicating the camera is stationary and the only real motion is the hands' playing.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the guinea pig came to be on the keyboard and whether it reacts or moves after the clip ends.
The musical piece or specific notes being played.
Any action that began before t=0 or continues after t=2.67 (the hands are already mid-phrase at the start and still playing at the end).
uncertain_details: Whether the guinea pig blinks or breathes visibly is hard to confirm at this frame rate.
Exact key presses per frame are approximate; some finger positions are partly occluded by the hand itself.
